title: Monomial basis of the explicit rational Verma quotient
statement: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional split semisimple Lie algebra over $\mathbf Q$ [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], with a splitting maximal abelian subalgebra $\mathfrak h$. Use its root spaces, coroots and a simple-root base $\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\}$ in the explicit conventions of [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition]. Put $R^+=R\cap\mathbf Z_{\ge0}\Delta$ and $\mathfrak n^\pm=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in R^+}\mathfrak g_{\pm\alpha}$. Let $U$ be the associative unital rational algebra generated linearly by $\mathfrak g$ with relations $xy-yx=[x,y]$. For any $\eta\in\mathfrak h^\vee$, let $I_\eta$ be the left ideal generated by $\mathfrak n^+$ and the elements $h-\eta(h)1$ for $h\in\mathfrak h$, and put $M(\eta)=U/I_\eta$ and $v_\eta=1+I_\eta$. This is a $\mathfrak g$-representation by left multiplication, $v_\eta\ne0$, $hv_\eta=\eta(h)v_\eta$, and $\mathfrak n^+v_\eta=0$. Choose any ordering $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_N$ of $R^+$ and nonzero $y_j\in\mathfrak g_{-\beta_j}$. Then $$y_1^{a_1}\cdots y_N^{a_N}v_\eta\quad(a_j\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0})$$ is a rational basis of $M(\eta)$, consisting of ordinary simultaneous $\mathfrak h$-eigenvectors of weights $\eta-\sum_j a_j\beta_j$. Thus $M(\eta)$ is generated by $v_\eta$, all its weights lie in $\eta-\mathbf Z_{\ge0}\Delta$, its $\eta$-weight space is exactly $\mathbf Qv_\eta$, and every weight space is finite-dimensional. For an empty root set the basis consists of $v_\eta$ alone.

source.place: Section 23h, printed p.508 (weight gradation), p.511, proof of Corollary 23.73 (need for fundamental highest weights). Missing background source: Serre, Complex Semisimple Lie Algebras, Chapter VII, Verma construction and ordinary PBW theorem, WANTED. The explicit left-ideal quotient fixes the rational model, rather than an unspecified descent from C.

proof.text: Choose a rational basis $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ of $\mathfrak h$ and nonzero $x_j\in\mathfrak g_{\beta_j}$. By [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition], the ordered list $(y_1,\ldots,y_N,t_1,\ldots,t_r,x_1,\ldots,x_N)$ is a basis of $\mathfrak g$, and $\mathfrak n^+$ is a Lie subalgebra. Also $[\mathfrak h,\mathfrak n^+]\subseteq\mathfrak n^+$ by the root-space definition, and $[\mathfrak h,\mathfrak h]=0$. Hence $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ is a finite-dimensional rational Lie subalgebra with $[\mathfrak b,\mathfrak b]\subseteq\mathfrak n^+$. The linear map $\chi(h+x)=\eta(h)$ vanishes on brackets, so [lem-sfb-enveloping-universal-property], applied to $L=\mathfrak b$ and $A=\mathbf Q$, gives a unital algebra homomorphism $\chi:B=U(\mathfrak b)\to\mathbf Q$ extending it.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--511, rational weight-representation background; agent reconstruction of the explicit Verma quotient argument, with Serre Chapter VII WANTED (not a claim that Milne proves PBW or the Verma construction).

proof.text: The inclusion $\mathfrak b\to\mathfrak g\to U$ extends to $B\to U$ by [lem-sfb-enveloping-universal-property]. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-pbw] first to $\mathfrak b$ with ordered basis $(t_i,x_j)$, then to $\mathfrak g$ with the ordered basis of step 1. The basis monomials $t^b x^c$ of $B$ map to a subset of the basis $y^a t^b x^c$ of $U$, so $B\to U$ is injective. Identify $B$ with its image. Grouping the full PBW expansion by $a$ gives a unique finite expansion $u=\sum_a y^a b_a$ with $b_a\in B$. Thus $U=\bigoplus_{a\in\mathbf N^N}y^a B$ as a right $B$-module. This uses arbitrary chosen nonzero root vectors and arbitrary root order; no Chevalley normalization or integrality of $\eta$ is required.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--511, rational weight-representation background; agent reconstruction of the explicit Verma quotient argument, with Serre Chapter VII WANTED (not a claim that Milne proves PBW or the Verma construction).

proof.text: Put $K=\ker\chi\subseteq B$. It is the left ideal of $B$ generated by $z-\chi(z)1$ for $z\in\mathfrak b$: each generator is in the kernel, and for a word $w=z_1\cdots z_m$ one has $$w-\chi(w)1=\sum_{i=1}^m z_1\cdots z_{i-1}(z_i-\chi(z_i)1)\prod_{j>i}\chi(z_j).$$ Every element of $B$ is a finite linear combination of words; if its character value is zero, subtracting the character values of those words expresses it in that left ideal. Since $z=h+x$ gives $z-\chi(z)1=(h-\eta(h)1)+x$, the generating family is equivalently $\mathfrak n^+$ together with all $h-\eta(h)1$. In particular $B/K\cong\mathbf Q$ via $\chi$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--511, rational weight-representation background; agent reconstruction of the explicit Verma quotient argument, with Serre Chapter VII WANTED (not a claim that Milne proves PBW or the Verma construction).

proof.text: The left ideal in the item is $I_\eta=UK$: the two inclusions follow from the common generators in step 3. In the unique expansion of step 2, multiplying by an element of $K$ on the right gives coefficients in $K$, since $K$ is an ideal of $B$. Conversely, every finite sum $\sum_a y^a k_a$ with $k_a\in K$ belongs to $UK$. Therefore $$I_\eta=\bigoplus_a y^a K.$$ The linear map $\sum_a y^a b_a\mapsto\sum_a\chi(b_a)e_a$ to the vector space with basis $(e_a)_{a\in\mathbf N^N}$ is surjective and has exactly this kernel. It induces a linear isomorphism $M(\eta)\cong\bigoplus_a\mathbf Q e_a$ sending $y^a v_\eta$ to $e_a$. These vectors are consequently a basis, and $v_\eta\ne0$.

proof.text: Left multiplication descends to $U/I_\eta$ because $I_\eta$ is a left ideal. For $z,z'\in\mathfrak g$ the defining relation gives $z(z'm)-z'(zm)=[z,z']m$, so this is a Lie representation in the sense of [def-wf-lie-algebra]. The generators of $I_\eta$ give $hv_\eta=\eta(h)v_\eta$ and $\mathfrak n^+v_\eta=0$. Every class is $uv_\eta$; since $U$ is generated linearly by $\mathfrak g$, the span of iterated $\mathfrak g$-actions on $v_\eta$ is all of $M(\eta)$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--511, rational weight-representation background; agent reconstruction of the explicit Verma quotient argument, with Serre Chapter VII WANTED (not a claim that Milne proves PBW or the Verma construction).

proof.text: The root-space definition in [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition] gives $[h,y_j]=-\beta_j(h)y_j$. In any associative algebra $[h,uv]=[h,u]v+u[h,v]$ by expanding both sides. Induction on the number of factors therefore gives $$[h,y_1^{a_1}\cdots y_N^{a_N}]=-\left(\sum_j a_j\beta_j(h)\right)y_1^{a_1}\cdots y_N^{a_N}.$$ Apply this to $v_\eta$ and use step 5: $h(y^av_\eta)=(\eta-\sum_j a_j\beta_j)(h)y^av_\eta$ for every $h$. Thus the displayed basis consists of ordinary simultaneous eigenvectors.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--511, rational weight-representation background; agent reconstruction of the explicit Verma quotient argument, with Serre Chapter VII WANTED (not a claim that Milne proves PBW or the Verma construction).

proof.text: For any functional $\mu$, expand a simultaneous eigenvector as the finite sum $m=\sum_a c_a y^a v_\eta$. Comparing basis coefficients in $hm=\mu(h)m$ for every $h$ gives $c_a(\eta-\sum_j a_j\beta_j-\mu)(h)=0$ for every $h$. If $c_a\ne0$, division by $c_a\in\mathbf Q$ forces $\mu=\eta-\sum_j a_j\beta_j$. Conversely every basis vector with that weight is a $\mu$-eigenvector. Hence the $\mu$-weight space has precisely the basis indexed by $\sum_j a_j\beta_j=\eta-\mu$; it is zero when this equation has no solution.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--511, rational weight-representation background; agent reconstruction of the explicit Verma quotient argument, with Serre Chapter VII WANTED (not a claim that Milne proves PBW or the Verma construction).

proof.text: The simple roots are a rational basis, and each $\beta_j$ has nonnegative integer coordinates $c_{ij}$, at least one positive, by the conventions of [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition]. Thus every occurring weight lies in $\eta-\mathbf Z_{\ge0}\Delta$. If $\sum_j a_j\beta_j=0$, the sum of its simple-root coordinates is $\sum_j a_j d_j=0$ with $d_j=\sum_i c_{ij}\ge1$, forcing every $a_j=0$. Step 7 then gives $M(\eta)_\eta=\mathbf Q v_\eta$. For any occurring weight $\mu$, put $H=\sum_i (\eta-\mu)_i\in\mathbf N$. Every tuple indexing its weight space satisfies $\sum_j a_jd_j=H$, hence $0\le a_j\le H$ for each $j$. There are at most $(H+1)^N$ such tuples, proving finite-dimensionality. Nonoccurring weights have zero space. If $N=0$, $\mathbf N^0$ contains just the empty tuple, so steps 2--7 give the single basis vector $v_\eta$ and all conclusions still hold.
